column2: Cloud service provider should ensure penetration testing had been performed on the cloud service covering best practises including OWASP top vulnerabilities, CWE Top 25 software errors, threats/vulnerabilities specific to microservices/API (where applicable) etc.
column6:
Microsoft performs security testing, including penetration testing, as part of its Security Development Lifecycle (SDL). All Microsoft software development teams are required to follow SDL requirements, which incorporate security requirements, threat-informed design, code review, automated security testing and penetration testing. Microsoft performs security testing, including penetration testing, across applicable Microsoft Azure infrastructure, services, and applications. Microsoft's Azure security guidance incorporates recognized industry practices, including OWASP Top 10 and API-specific security risks such as those identified in the OWASP API Security Top 10.The exact testing methodology and scope are service-specific and determined based on the applicable architecture and attack surface.

Azure – Commercial – Penetration Testing Report and Azure + Dynamics 365 + Online Services – Public & Government SOC 2 Type II Report are available.

column2: Authentication
Does the cloud service supports and enable integration with the Bank's Azure Active Directory (AD) for all interactive user authentication?
column6: Yes. All Azure services listed are governed by Microsoft Entra ID, which is the Bank's Azure AD tenant. Interactive access via the Azure Portal, CLI l is authenticated against Entra ID and authorised by Azure RBAC. Users are federated to the Bank's AD DS

(b) Passwords which have been used for the last 5 changes (configurable) should not be reused.

User passwords should be protected from disclosure if it needs to be printed. This includes supporting the following controls:

(a) Ensuring clear-text password is not exposed before reaching the printer.

(b) Ink ribbon shall not be used for password printing.

(c) Printed password shall not be visible on surface of password mailer.

(d) Password mailer shall be tampered evident.

(e) Password shall be printed direct without the need for a spoof file.

column2: Data Security

Only cryptographic algorithms / standards which are of established international standards such as National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) and subjected to rigorous scrutiny by an international communicty of cryptographers, or approved by authoritative professional bodies or government agencies, should be used for the protection of sensitive information and credentials.

Such algorithms include RSA-2048bit, AES-128bit and above, SHA256 and above, etc.

column2: When the cloud service leverages on multi-tenanted architecture like sharing of computes/storage/network resources with other entities, please provide details of logical and physical controls to protect bank's data comingling in storage and in processing.
column6:
Logical controls (storage + processing isolation): Azure FedRAMP states tenant separation is enforced through VLAN segmentation, ACL-based deny-by-default flow control, host/VM firewalls, and VFP filtering between tenant assets; and VM processing isolation is enforced by hypervisor separation of Host/Guest OS and Guest-to-Guest boundaries. For storage, Azure documents encryption at rest (AES-256, FIPS 140-2), TLS in transit, AD security-group least-privilege access, and ACLs preventing storage hosts from external exposure. Azure SOC corroborates this with tested controls for tenant segregation and storage confidentiality (LA-3, LA-4), with no exceptions noted in the sampled tests.
Physical controls (protecting underlying shared infrastructure): Azure FedRAMP documents PE controls including 24x7 guarded single-entry datacenters, MFA physical access (badge + biometrics/mantraps), continuous CCTV/alarm monitoring, access logging/review, and restricted server/caged areas with least privilege. Azure SOC Section 4 Physical & Environmental Security similarly reports PE control testing over access restrictions, surveillance, and quarterly access reviews; one period showed two datacenter physical-access mechanism exceptions, with follow-up sampling noting no additional exceptions.

column2: Network Security

Where the solution requires access and/or communication to/from the public Internet:-

a) A multi-tier network architecture (comprising of untrusted network, DMZ, trusted network zone for Internet-based application and  internal systems) shall be implemented.

b) Direct connections between untrusted network and trusted network shall not be allowed. External users (in untrusted network) should only have access to the external-facing service in DMZ network. 

(iii) Business logic and non-public data should not reside in the DMZ segment
column6: Azure environment supports multi-tier architecture (VNet subnets, NSGs, Azure Firewall, Front Door + WAF). No public-facing web servers currently exist, so no DMZ is required now. If Internet-facing workloads are deployed, a DMZ architecture will be implemented.

column2:
Where the solution requires access and/or communication from/to external party via private leased line (semi-trusted network):-

(i) A multi-tier network architecture (comprising of semi-trusted network, DMZ and bank trusted network) shall be implemented. The DMZ shall act as a staging area between external systems and the systems within trusted network. 

(ii) Direct connections from semi-trusted network (to the trusted network) shall not be allowed.

(iii) DMZ-based devices should be vigilantly maintained (i.e., patched)
column6: No third-party integrations currently exis. When introduced, they will use ExpressRoute or Virtual WAN with a segregated DMZ subnet, firewall inspection and NSGs.
